thread:
maria: FYI we just got a DSAR from a EU customer asking for full deletion of all PII, includes archived snapshots in us-west and eu-west. they specifically asked for proof of deletion.
ashwin: thanks — do we know if any snapshots are encrypted with customer-keystore keys that were rotated/retired? that can affect ability to prove crypto-delete.
david: quick check: found 3 related snapshots across accounts — two in eu-west, one in us-west. The us-west one is tagged `cust:EU-1234` and references KMS key `projects/redwood/keys/cust-eu-1234-v1`.
maria: hmm that key was scheduled for rotation in feb but not destroyed. could rotation have left any orphaned encrypted blobs?
ashwin: if the key was rotated (new version) but old version still active, decryption should work. if the key was disabled/destroyed that's a problem. can we confirm key state?
david: checked KMS audit logs: `kms.updateCryptoKeyVersion` shows a destroy scheduled on 2025-11-09 for version 1 but `kms.destroyCryptoKeyVersion` was never called; however the key policy changed and a service account used by snapshot-restore lost “cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt” temporarily on 2026-01-14.
maria: that matches support ticket from Jan where a restore failed for a dev environment. So it's plausible some automated backfills couldn't decrypt snapshots during that window.
ashwin: ok, from a DSAR angle: we need to (1) determine whether the blobs are actually still present in storage, (2) confirm whether we can decrypt for verification, (3) if not decryptable, we need an evidence-backed retention exception or documented proof of irretrievability.
elaine: legal here — for EU DSAR we must provide evidence of deletion or a formal refusal with justification. If data is irrecoverable due to key destruction, we still must document chain-of-custody and KMS logs showing key material disposal. A retention exception is different — do not invent one.
maria: proposal: create a short runbook: a) snapshot inventory (ids + regions + tags) b) KMS key audit (versions + IAM events) c) storage object checksums + blob retention state d) attempt controlled decrypt with audit logging e) if decrypt fails, collect KMS lifecycle logs and timeline for legal.
ashwin: I'll own (b) and (d). david, can you own (a) and (c)? ops, can you escalate a read-only RBAC exception for the `snapshot-audit` service account to allow decryption attempts? we want temporary `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt` only and logged.
david: yes but need approval from infra-owners. I'll open a short-lived change request: `CR-2026-041` with scope and TTL 4h. I'll attach the command snippet:
```
# grant temporary decrypt to snapshot-audit-sa
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood --member=serviceAccount:snapshot-audit@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
# revoke after tests
```
ops: ack — please include `ops@redwood` in the CR for emergency rollback. We'll run decryption attempts in a sealed audit session.
security-bot: Incident policy triggered: potential data availability issue flagged. Created incident INC-2026-511. Please reference in CR. :exclamation:
maria: also, we need to be careful about proof of deletion. If we can decrypt and then delete, we should record deletion transactions and storage-level object removal (and replication confirmation in other regions). If we cannot decrypt, we should get an attestation from KMS logs that key material no longer exists.
ashwin: one more gotcha: snapshots may exist in offsite backup chains (tapes/snapshots from third-party backup provider) beyond our immediate blobstore. david, do we have contract/legal visibility for those providers?
david: checking — backup provider `vaultline` has longer retention; we have an agreement that allows deletes on request but it requires an API call. I'll include them in the CR and cc legal.
elaine: please cc privacy@legal and attach customer DSAR copy. We will coordinate whether a partial redaction + deletion timeline is acceptable or a full erasure proof is required.
maria: timeline: try to run inventory + KMS audit in next 24h, request temporary RBAC CR today, attempt decrypt tests within 48h, and send interim update to customer. Does that sound reasonable?
ashwin: that's fine. I'll also add an audit trap: all decrypt attempts should be captured by our audit pipeline (stackdriver + immutable log export) and hashed into the DSAR evidence bundle.
david: opened CR-2026-041 and linked INC-2026-511. added TTL 4h, change window tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Link: https://cr.redwood.internal/CR-2026-041
maria: great. one more: if decryption succeeds and we delete, we must also consider embedding indexes and any derived artifacts. add a checklist item to search embeddings tables for `cust:EU-1234` and schedule purge.
nashwin: noted — will run targeted embedding queries after snapshot validation. keep in mind some embeddings are replicated to analytics read-replicas; include DB purge + replica sync confirmation.
elaine: keep me posted before you send proof to the requester. If any refusal is needed, we need a legal signoff and a standardized refusal letter template.
ops: I'll be on standby for RBAC rollback and will capture the audit bundle.
maria: thanks team — tagging @david @ashwin @elaine @ops. I'll post an interim summary to the DSAR tracker after the decrypt attempt. :thumbsup:
